state: The maintenance example needs reliable template supersession and equipment retirement for the same sizes: 99, 100, 101 and 1000 separate plan/check records. Today Plan.update cancels future pending checks in an atomic loop capped at 100; Asset.update retirement caps both its plan loop and each check loop at 100, causing rollback when either exceeds that bound. A dynamic Plan invariant requires a currently eligible technician and an unretired asset, making asynchronous deactivation incompatible with the stored invariant. Keep immutable occurrence, checklist, assigned inspector and completed evidence, and retain work whose due day had already arrived when a manager changed the plan or retired the asset. Future pending instances must instead be canceled with that manager's attribution. Losing present role/employment cannot invalidate old evidence, but present eligibility must govern new plan admission, schedule generation, reminder release and inspection use. If an old cleanup request runs after another plan edit or asset reinstatement, it must neither restore the old prospective work nor cancel fresh occurrences. Work per atomic operation cannot scale with unrelated records; normal local finite bounds still apply. The language already has owned models/evidence records, pure decisions, hooks, committed identity events, keyed deadlines, record-ID continuations and scoped manual recovery. There is no authored historic-audit query or queue introspection API to substitute for business evidence. Resource downtime, restoration and affected booking review remain exclusively CanRent's. No general coordination layer, scheduler, copied reservation store or multi-owner atomicity is authorized. Assess the Can draft and desired JavaScript freely rather than preserving prototype limitations.

progress.instructions: Which alternative best preserves all the listed business outcomes with the least justified complexity? Judge each against the identical requirements, and disclose uncertainty rather than treating a queued acknowledgement as completion.

criteria.atomic_caps: Keep the two bounded fanout hooks as they stand, along with the invariant that an active configuration always has a valid present assignee and nonretired parent. Managers would have to arrange smaller edits to avoid rollback. It provides immediate local completion and avoids new stored facts, but fails the specified larger inventories and allows changing staff eligibility to obstruct preservation of old plan state.
criteria.event_only: Make each hook finite and express continuing cleanup as typed events carrying original cutoff, version/generation and attribution. Eligibility checks move out of the historical invariant. Do not persist an invalidation record. This avoids an evidence entity; however, admitting work against only the current mutable template/retirement facts loses earlier boundaries after subsequent changes, and there is no ordinary record for a manager to inspect/retry if event progress was missed.
criteria.owned_evidence: Persist an immutable invalidation fact at the maintenance owner for every real edit/retirement: former plan version or former asset retirement generation, the change-day cutoff, author/time and reason. New inspections freeze the asset generation, advanced by each retirement. Keep next-record cursor and completion status on that fact, cancel matching pending future records one at a time, and reject already invalidated prospective use before physical cleanup. Completed facts continue protecting the historical boundary. A scoped owner action retries the same fact. This adds localized evidence/generation/queries, in exchange for visible attributable backlog, safe resumption and immunity to later template changes or asset reinstatement without modifying Rent availability.
